This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant as he has been arrested on 08.07.2023 in connection with Crime No.377/2023 registered at Police Station Jhansi Road, District Gwalior for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376, 506, 120-B of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

3. Prosecution case, in brief, is that on 01.02.2023 at about 14:00 hours, when prosecutrix was returning to her house and reached near Chandravadni Naka, co-accused Veeru met her and on false pretext to drop her at her home got her seated on his motorcycle and took her to Cancer Pahadiya Abhishek Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171543934/
1 Forest, where applicant was present.

entities.text: Cancer Pahadiya Abhishek Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant sexually assaulted her and threatened to kill her if she narrated the incident to anybody.

During investigation, she in her statement recorded on 01.07.2023 under Section 164 of CrPC stated that on the date of incident, co-accused Jeetu was also present on the spot, who made video recording of the incident, whereafter they threatened her to blackmail her by making the video of the incident viral and demanded money from the prosecutrix.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that admittedly, the FIR was lodged after about 4 months' of the incident.
Prosecutrix was major at the time of incident as nothing has been produced with regard to her age.
Her statement made before the Investigating Officer as well as the doctor who conducted her MLC, are inconsistent with her own FIR on material issues.
She was a consenting party.
The applicant has falsely been implicated in the matter.

The co-accused Jeetu has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 10.10.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.44947/2023.
He is in custody since 08.07.2023.
The investigation has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed.
Trial will take time to conclude

; therefore, under these circumstances,
applicant is entitled for bail.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that applicant is the main accused who sexually assaulted the minor prosecutrix.
The offence alleged against applicant is serious in nature, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.

6. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.
7.

Having considered rival submissions, material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant with regard to age of prosecutrix, the delayed FIR and the fact that investigation has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed and other facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Aman Abhishek Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171543934/
